join_order.notes: branch[partkey] direct-array lookup; partkey is dense int32 0..2M, use array not hash

branch_array.description: branch[partkey] = 0 (no match), 1 (Brand#12/SM), 2 (Brand#23/MED), 3 (Brand#34/LG). Built from single scan of part table.

quantity_ranges.description: quantity_ranges[branch] = {lo, hi}. Branch 0 unused. Branch 1: [1,11], Branch 2: [10,20], Branch 3: [20,30].

thread_accumulators.description: Per-thread partial SUM, final reduce after parallel scan

build_branch_array.description: Single-pass scan of part table to populate branch[] array
steps: Load p_brand_dict, p_container_dict; resolve dict codes for Brand#12, Brand#23, Brand#34 and all 12 container values
Scan p_partkey, p_brand, p_container, p_size in parallel (small table, use all threads)
For each part row: check brand+container+size against all 3 branches, write branch[partkey] = matching branch (1/2/3) or 0

scan_lineitem.description: Parallel scan of lineitem with early filter on shipinstruct+shipmode, then branch lookup
filter_order: 2. l_shipmode == air_code || l_shipmode == airreg_code (int8 compare, 13% pass)

parallelism.notes: Part table build is fast (2M rows), can be single-threaded or lightly parallel. Lineitem scan is the bottleneck — fully parallel with per-thread accumulators.

mmap_strategy.notes: Demand-paged mmap for all column files. MADV_SEQUENTIAL for lineitem columns (full scan). Declare mmap resources before RAII timer to exclude munmap TLB shootdown.

indexes.purpose: NOT USED — sequential part scan + direct branch_array is faster than random index lookups

vectorization_hints.notes: Use __restrict__ on all column pointers for auto-vectorization. The shipinstruct+shipmode check is two int8 compares — highly vectorizable.
